description.narrative: Programme Sector(s): Emergency Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene promotion (WASH) Response with, Gender and protection mainstreamed. Oxfam has been working in Uganda since 1963 implementing both humanitarian and development programs across the country, with a recent focus on humanitarian response and preparedness, Resilience strengthening, supporting resilient livelihoods, peaceful co-existence and inclusive livelihoods, women rights and gender justice and accountable governance. Oxfam’s Humanitarianwork has been focusing in northern Uganda for South Sudan refuge response (in West Nile and Mid-North); Congolese Refugee Response in Southwest; and IDPs response in Elgon region, where we have focused on increasing access to safe water and sanitation facilities as well as hygiene promotion, gender and protection, and emergency food security <(>&<)> livelihoods. In Mt Elgon region, Oxfam started operation in 2022 after the flash floods and mud slides disaster that affected communities in Mbale city, Mbale district, Bulambuli and Butaleja districts and as such Oxfam has remained very active in the region. Currently, Oxfam in Consortium with Uganda Red Cross Society and Caritas Tororo is implementing disaster preparedness project titled “Early Warning, Early Action: Strengthening Multi-hazard Disaster Preparedness” project funded by ECHO. This project aims at building on previous DG ECHO funded project, on ongoing government efforts, existing local structures and previous experiences in 7 target districts (Bududa, Butaleja, Mbale, Namisindwa, and Sironko and Bulambuli and Mbale City) in the Mount Elgon region in Eastern Uganda, through interventions designed to strengthen multi-hazard disaster preparedness in the region. The region continues to experience increased extreme events (floods) leading to disasters affecting people’s lives, livelihoods and economic disruption. Description of the crisis (including number of affected, timeline, number of affected Oxfam has reached to date etc.): The Mt. Elgon region of Eastern Uganda is highly prone to climate induced disasters associated with heavy rainfall, including floods, landslides, hailstorms, and soil mass wasting/movement. Its unique topography, comprising highland, mid-highland, and low-lying zones, exposescommunities to multiple and overlapping risks. The highlands are particularly susceptible to landslides, falling boulders, and deep cracks, while mid-highland areas face debris flows, crop destruction, and infrastructure damage. The low-lying zones oftenexperience widespread flooding, siltation, and prolonged dry spells that severely impact agricultural production and food security. In late August 2025, Elgon region was hit by intense rainfall that lasted for several hours resulting in flash floods, and mudslides, as a result, several riverbanks busted due to the heavy downpour. This led to destruction of homes, submerged water and sanitation infrastructures, displacement of families, and widespread disruption of livelihoods in Mbale City, Mbale, Butaleja, Bududa, Namisindwa, Manafwa, Bulambuli and Sironko District. Preliminary rapid assessments conducted by the Districts and City Disaster Management Committees of Mbale city, Mbale district, Bulambuli, Butaleja and Sironko District, with support from Uganda Red Cross Society (URCS) and other partners, highlighted significant impacts on households (over 5,883 HH and over 17,434 individuals) were displaced/affected with 3 death registered and over 78 people severely injured, over 770 acres of agricultureland/farms were destroyed, water and sanitation infrastructure were destroyed and submerged, education facilities, and road networks. According to the Uganda National Meteorological Authority (UNMA), weather outlook (SOND), the region will continue to receive heavy rainfall with the highest peak of rainfall which will be above the normal trend thus this will still create high chances of increased flooding and landslide events in the Mt Elgon sub region. Currently most of the areas in the High-altitude zonesare soggy with water oozing from the ground at different points. This is an indicator of the increased risk of landslides in these areas, and all the lowlands are flooded. Access to safe water remained hindered as most of the water supply infrastructures such as existing gravity flow schemes with public water tap stands, springs and boreholes as main safe water sources have been affected with the floodingimpact, landslide leading to access to unsafe water for drinking and other domestic use from unprotected and open water sources which are deemed to be contaminated, With collapsed sanitation facilities both at institutional and household level and poor waste management resulting from the flooding, contamination of ground water is anticipated to be higher due to continued seepage, Moist Low lying areas are not suitable for sinking latrines given the loose nature of soils as well as high water table prevailing risk of open defecation. Over 685 HH and institutional latrines are destroyed and submergedwhich continues to post risk of increasing risk of open water sources (springs and borehole) from contamination. The significant damage/destruction of water and sanitation infrastructures consequently presents a serious public health risk as communitiescontinued to fetch water from unsafe sources, have no access to latrine, open defecation, contamination as a result of seepage of sewage, poor hygiene practice and negative coping mechanism , in addition, these situations leads to increase in Gender Based Violence (GBV) within households and tensions at water sources as well asprotection risks as a result of women and girls walking long distances in search of clean water. Generally, there is very minimal support from partners and Government, OPM has only provided food assistance and Oxfam through its partner (URCS and Caritas) and other partners have distributed some basic assistance such as shelter items and cash for other basic household items. The needs on ground are anonymous including limited access to adequate safe water, dignified sanitary facilities, soap, water collection and storage containers, water treatment tablets, limited access to digging tools <(>&<)> hygiene kits, solid waste management challenges and the need for community engagement on behavioral change regarding key hygiene and sanitation practices. Project description / activities (including numbers to be reached): Oxfam proposes to implement an integrated WASH, Gender and Protection, project that addresses thecurrent needs of the floods and mudslide affected people in the selected districts of Sironko, Mbale, Butaleja and Bulambuli districts in close collaboration with OPM and with respective DDMCs and partners. The project is expected to reach a total of 30,000 (Females-15,300, Males- 14,700) individuals and will be building on on-going response initiatives by Oxfam on disaster risk reduction especially anticipatory and early warning and other players. The project aims to enable the disaster affected communities to access basic WaSH services within the recommended Sphere and government standards while strengthening their resilience and self-reliance. Oxfam will enhance access to safe water, dignified sanitary facilities and hygiene practices through community engagement on behavioral change and building resilience for mitigation of re-occurrence among the disaster affected communities in synergy with OPM, DDMCs, district/ city line departments and partners targeting both community and institutional intervention. Water supply: Actions will target repair and upgrade of mine water systems, rehabilitation of broken-down bore holes, damaged pipelines and protected springs within the affected areas, installation of water storage tanks in institutions, procure and pre-position pool testers and DPD tablets forwater quality monitoring, provision of chlorine for water treatment, support the district water department conduct detailed water quality monitoring and provision of water collection and storage containers and upgrading of mine water systems. Sanitation: Access to safe excreta systems at communal level will include construction of 30 gender sensitive communal latrines and 20 bath shelters, construction and distribution of dome shaped slabs to 400 individuals for HH latrine construction, procurement and distribution of 150sets of latrines digging tools for pit excavation, provision of latrine cleaning kit including detergents. Additionally, the project will support in establishment and strengthening of solid waste management structuresthrough training and provision of PPEs, environmental cleaning kits and Mobile Bins for appropriate solid waste management, construction of 5 blocks of 5 stances climate resilient and gender sensitive institutional latrines. safety/protection and menstrual hygiene management, and promotion of safe hygiene andsanitation practices at institutions through child-to-child approaches. Hygiene promotion: Oxfam will strengthen capacity and empower community structures and volunteers with relevant skillson participatory approaches and tools to mobilize the targeted affected communities to adhere to proper hygiene and sanitation practices to mitigate diarrheal diseases, women and girls within the menstrualage group will be supported with menstrual hygiene kits, the project will procure an distribute both institutional and HH level hand washing facilities for hand washing practices, hygiene promotion campaigns on safe excreta disposal, solid waste management, hand washing and safe water chain management will beundertaken through radio talks shows, Development, reproduction and dissemination of IEC materials. As an immediate and intermediate measure, Oxfam will continue to positively engage school children and Teachers as agents of change. In addition, Oxfam will engage with school management committees and Parent-Teachers Associations on appropriate operation and maintenance of the WASH facilities established in schools. Mainstreaming of Gender: Protection and Environmental management initiatives will be prioritized across all interventions. Oxfam will also use this intervention to engage the DDMCs at district level on enhancing community awareness on early warning/ early response initiatives. This funding will provide leverage for scale up of similar interventions under the ECHO-DP that also includes Cash Transfer initiatives for early response which is currently running in five other districts of Mt Elgon region. Summary of proposed Activities. Water supply: - Pipeline extension and re-instating ofdamaged pipelines for 1.0km, repair and rehabilitation of nonfunctional tap water sources - Upgrade/repair of mini water system (fixing of electromechanics components, solar system repair) - Full repair and rehabilitation of 6 handpumps. - Rehabilitation and protection of 2 natural springs - Installation of 02 rainwater harvesting facilities in schools and health center facilities. - Procurement and distribution of water treatment tablets (Aqua tablets). - Pre-positioning of water treatmentchemicals (HTH Chlorine) - Support in capacity building of water management committees. Oxfam will work with DWO to strengthen the capacities of WUCs - Conduct water sources functionality mapping. Sanitation: - Construction of 2 blocks of 3 stances climate resilient institutional drainable latrines. - Support construction of 100 HH latrines using dome-sharp slabs. - Support construction of 10 gender sensitive Flood resistantlatrines (Eco-Toilet/Tiger worm) for vulnerable HH. - Procurement and distribution of 15 sets of latrines digging tools for pit excavation - Procurement and distribution of 15 branded mobile bins for waste management. - Conduct Institutional WASH assessment survey. Hygiene promotion - Procurement and installation of 15 bulk Hand washing facilities for communal latrines, health facilities and other community meeting places. - Procurement and distribution of 200 water collection and storage containers for vulnerable households. - Procurement and distribution of 15 sets of environmental and latrine cleaning materials (liquid soap, jik, Metallic Bucket, hard brush, slashes, hoe, wheelbarrow) - Procure and distribute 20 usable dignity kits for vulnerable women and girls (1 bar of soap,2 knickers, 1 packet of Afri pads, 1 lesu - 1.5 meters, 1 branded cloth bag), this will enhance dignified and proper management of menstrual hygiene. - Procurement and distribution of laundry soap vulnerable affected persons (white star - 1 kg), this will at least target high risk categories of the community including PSNs, VHTs and hygienists to facilitate personal and hand hygiene practicesto prevent disease outbreaks. - Training and equipping patrons, matrons and schools’ health clubs on CHAST approach and provision of CHAST Tools (CHAST Tools, Stationaries, Tool kits, Meals, facilitators allowances, Hall hire, etc). At least 5 schools health clubs comprising of 90 club members i.e. 30 ( 15 boys and 15 girls each) - will be trained and equipped with CHAST tools to enhance hygiene and sanitation practices among learners in the targeted schools, approaches appreciates children as changes agents and are expected to cascade hygiene and sanitation practice learnt at school in their homes and the community at large for improved behavior change. - Development, Reproduction of assorted IEC materials (flyers, Stickers, T-shirts, Billboards etc) depicting key messages on Health and good hygiene and sanitation practices as well as messages on proper operation and maintenance of the sanitaryfacilities, gender desegregation stickers for communal latrines. These will complement other key initiatives of risk communication and community engagement to foster behaviour change for improved health, sanitation and hygiene among the targeted communities and institutions. - Conduct Radio talk show on key Health concerns, hygiene and sanitation practices (Hand washing, Latrine use and maintenance, safe water management). The project will facilitate key stakeholders such as District line departments, DDMC for targeted districts to conduct 2 radio talk shows (each district allocated 3 shows) geared towards increasing risk communications on Mpox prevention, early warning for people still in high-risk areas and awareness among the targeted communities. - Conduct 4 community dialogue meetings (1 perdistrict) with affected communities on key health, hygiene and sanitation practices, early warming, anticipatory actions, gender and protection). This will enhance a two ways information, feedback sharing, and engagement to facilitate community led action plan formulation and monitoring of key health, sanitation and hygiene practices among the targeted communities. These platforms will enhance accountability, inclusiveness, empower local community structuresto act and GBV prevention. - The project will engage and equip 40VHTs for community engagement and social mobilization of key health concerns, sanitation and hygiene concerns, including early warning Incentives for 40 VHTs for 4 months. This will complement other risk communication and community engagement initiatives such dialogues, radio talk shows, for realization of improve positive behaviour change among the targeted communities. - Procurement of 10 megaphones to support community structures during awareness raising campaign - Conduct a gender and protection / Risk Analysis, this ai in generating key gender and protection concern and risks to inform an inclusive WaSH programming. - Conduct PDM and KAP survey - Documentation and publication. Any unspent funds by this date (whether loan or grant) will be returned.  I will provide a monthly update of total spend  For grants, I will provide an End of Implementation report– a simple narrative and financial report (template provided) within 3 months from the end of the period of use.  For loans, at the end of project I will provide a brief summary describing what the CAT fund loan enabled the programme to do while awaiting other funds.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
